record.paper_title: Open problems in deformations of Artinian algebras, Hilbert schemes and around
record.original_question: For every pair (n, d), is the very compressed locus VC_{n,d} either contained in the smoothable component of Hilb_d(A^n) or itself an irreducible component?

evidence.quote: Problem XV. Is the following alternative true for all (n, d): VCn,d lies in the smoothable component or it forms a component?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$. For positive integers $n$ and $d$, let $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ denote the Hilbert scheme parameterizing zero-dimensional closed subschemes of length $d$ in affine $n$-space $\mathbb{A}^n_k$. The smoothable component $\mathrm{Hilb}_d^{\mathrm{sm}}(\mathbb{A}^n) \subseteq \mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ is the closure of the open locus parameterizing $d$ distinct reduced points.

A finite local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak{m},k)$ of length $d$ with Hilbert function $h_A = (h_0, h_1, \dots, h_s)$, where $h_i = \dim_k(\mathfrak{m}^i/\mathfrak{m}^{i+1})$ and $s$ is the socle degree, is called very compressed if
$$h_i = \min\!\left(\binom{n+i-1}{i},\; d - \sum_{j<i} h_j - \sum_{j>i}\binom{n+s-j-1}{s-j}\right) \quad \text{for some embedding dimension } n.$$
Equivalently, the Hilbert function is the maximal one compatible with length $d$, embedding dimension $\le n$, and a fixed socle degree. Let $\mathrm{VC}_{n,d} \subseteq \mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n)$ denote the locally closed subscheme parameterizing subschemes supported at a single point whose local algebra is very compressed (taken over all admissible socle degrees), together with its standard scheme structure.

Question: Is it true that for every pair $(n,d)$, the very compressed locus $\mathrm{VC}_{n,d}$ either is contained in the smoothable component $\mathrm{Hilb}_d^{\mathrm{sm}}(\mathbb{A}^n)$, or else is itself an irreducible component of $\mathrm{Hilb}_d(\mathbb{A}^n)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on components of Hilbert schemes of low degree (e.g., a December 2025 preprint analyzing degrees 9 and 10 and Hilbert functions such as (1,5,3) and (1,6,3)) provides progress on related questions about elementary components and the very compressed locus, but does not establish the full alternative for all pairs (n,d). No source found resolves the dichotomy in general.

status_evidence.title: Components of Hilbert Schemes of low degree and smoothable algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Studies elementary components for degrees 9 and 10 with Hilbert functions (1,5,3) and (1,6,3); addresses related but distinct open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on related questions; the general very compressed locus alternative remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: New elementary components of the Gorenstein locus of the Hilbert scheme of points
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs new elementary (non-smoothable) components of Hilbert schemes via very compressed/Gorenstein algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Examples of very compressed loci forming components exist; general dichotomy not proved.
